subject: Greenland
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about map projections. Claims are cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary). Map geometry comes from Natural Earth and is not evidence for any claim.

claims.text: On the Mercator projection, Greenland appears the same size as Africa, when in reality Africa's area is 14 times as large.
Greenland's real area is comparable to the Democratic Republic of the Congo's alone.
The Mercator projection inflates the size of lands the farther they are from the equator, so Greenland and Antarctica appear far larger than they are.

Gerardus Mercator first presented the projection in 1569; in the 18th century it became the standard map projection for navigation, because it draws rhumb lines (constant compass bearings) as straight lines.
Its use for maps other than marine charts declined in the 20th century but resurged in the 21st century because of characteristics favourable for online mapping.
Geographica's maps are drawn in the Web Mercator projection.
Greenland's total area is 2,166,086 km2; Africa's is about 30.3 million km2.
Algeria, at 2,381,741 km2, is the largest country in Africa; the Democratic Republic of the Congo, at 2,345,408 km2, is the second largest. Both are larger than Greenland (2,166,086 km2).
